newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Caltex Philippines studies purchase of Iraqi crude.
newsitem.headline: Caltex Philippines studies purchase of Iraqi crude.

text.p: Caltex (Philippines) Inc is studying the possibility of buying Iraqi crude, a top official of the company said on Saturday.

"We are studying the economics and will probably decide by next week. Our consideration is that it should be competitive with other crude types," the official, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters.
The official said American oil companies were also required to seek clearance from the U.S. government before buying crude from Iraq.

"In the past, we have evaluated the economics and it did not appear to be good as it was more expensive than other crude types. We're of the thinking that this time there might be some incentive or it may be cheaper," the official said.
Some 85 percent of the crude requirements of the company are sourced from the Middle East while remaining supply comes from East Asian countries.
The official said that Caltex has contracted crude supply that will last up to January. It is operating a 72,000 bpd (barrels of oil per day) refinery in northern Philippines.
Caltex Philippines is the local unit of Caltex Petroleum Corp, a joint venture of Texaco Inc and Chevron Corp.
